survey: A round wall clock seen almost straight on, hanging on a flat wall with vertical stripes. The wall faces the camera directly; its stripes are vertical and parallel. The orange rim is a thick round ring. Its outer edge and the white dial inside it fit true ellipses with the same proportions (width ratio 0.95) and almost the same short axis (179° and 176°). So the rim and dial share one axis, and the clock is turned only very slightly away from straight on. The hour marks sit evenly around the dial: 12 and 6 are vertical, 3 and 9 are horizontal, and the others point toward the centre. At this nearly flat-on angle they barely need to shrink, and they don't. The minute dots follow the dial's edge evenly. The hour, minute and red second hands meet at one central hub that sits on the dial. A soft shadow below and to the left shows the clock resting flat against the wall, which matches the face-on wall. Everything fits one nearly frontal camera.
